items.bold: PROJECT FREEDOM WORKS: 2 US-FLAGGED MERCHANT VESSELS successfully transited Hormuz. CENTCOM confirmed.
items.text: Times of Israel (45 minutes ago) confirmed: CENTCOM posted on X — "As a first step, 2 US-flagged merchant vessels have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz and are safely headed on their journey." US Navy guided-missile destroyers are now operating in the Arabian Gulf after transiting Hormuz in support of Project Freedom. CENTCOM force committed: guided-missile destroyers, over 100 land and sea-based aircraft, multi-domain unmanned platforms, and 15,000 service members. This is the most significant Hormuz development since the brief April 17 opening. Two vessels through without Iranian attack = the ceasefire framework is holding under operational pressure. Iran blinked first.

items.bold: IRAN CLAIMED missile strike on US vessel near Jask. CENTCOM DENIED: "propaganda and false."
items.text: Fox News live (1 hour ago) confirmed: Iran's semi-official Fars News Agency (IRGC-linked) claimed two Iranian missiles hit an unidentified US vessel near the port of Jask. CENTCOM spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins issued an immediate denial: Iran's missile strike claims are "propaganda and false." No US vessel was struck. This is Iran's messaging strategy: claim a strike to maintain deterrence credibility without actually attacking and risking full war resumption. The false claim is significant: it shows Iran is not willing to actually attack Project Freedom vessels — but wants to maintain the perception that it could. For markets: the false claim temporarily spiked oil before CENTCOM denial pushed it back. Net result: Project Freedom operational, Iran did not attack, ceasefire holding.

items.bold: IRAN LAWMAKER AZIZI: US escort is "ceasefire violation." "Hormuz not managed by Trump's delusional posts."
items.text: Fox News live confirmed: Iranian senior lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi (head of Iran's Parliament National Security and Foreign Policy Committee) warned: "Any American interference in the new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz will be considered a violation of the ceasefire." Added: "The Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf would not be managed by Trump's delusional posts!" Azizi's warning positions Iran to escalate diplomatically while Project Freedom operates. However, the fact that Iran did NOT attack the 2 vessels that successfully transited — despite Azizi's warning — suggests Iran is choosing rhetoric over military action. The ceasefire framework is holding, at least for Day 1 of Project Freedom.

assessment.headline: DAY 66, 6:45PM MON: PROJECT FREEDOM WORKED — 2 US vessels transited Hormuz without incident. Iran did NOT attack. CENTCOM denied Iranian missile claim as "propaganda and false." Sensex +903 to 77,816. Brent $109. India must get into Project Freedom escort this week.
assessment.body:
Monday 6:45 PM IST. Day 66. Project Freedom delivered its first result.

PROJECT FREEDOM — DAY 1 OUTCOME
• 2 US-flagged merchant vessels successfully transited Hormuz (CENTCOM confirmed)
• US Navy guided-missile destroyers operating in Arabian Gulf
• Force deployed: 100+ aircraft, multi-domain drones, 15,000 service members
• Iran DID NOT ATTACK the vessels
• Iran claimed a missile strike — CENTCOM denied: "propaganda and false"
• Iran chose rhetoric over military action

WHAT IRAN'S RESTRAINT MEANS
• Iran positioned itself diplomatically (called it ceasefire violation)
• But did not escalate militarily
• This preserves the ceasefire framework even under direct operational pressure
• Iran may be keeping diplomatic track (14-point proposal) alive while protesting Project Freedom
• The Azizi "ceasefire violation" framing gives Iran a future escalation justification if it chooses
• But on Day 1: Iran blinked

THE DUAL TRACK
• Military: Project Freedom escorts 2 vessels through, 39 total redirected by blockade
• Diplomatic: Trump says "very positive discussions" with Iran continuing
• Both tracks running simultaneously — maximum pressure + maximum negotiation

INDIA'S MONDAY RESULT
• Sensex +903 to 77,816. Nifty +202 to 24,200
• Brent $109 — retreating from $126 peak
• HUL +4.4%, Vedanta +7.9%, Kotak Q4 beat
• Election stability: DMK TN, Congress Kerala, WB ongoing
• Rs 14L Cr added to BSE market cap in one session

THE INDIA ACTION REQUIRED
• MEA must engage US TODAY on Indian-flagged tanker inclusion in Project Freedom
• Kharif fertiliser: June planting is 6-8 weeks away — restart Gulf sourcing NOW
• OMC hike at $109: Rs 5-8/L (reduced from Rs 9-14/L at $126 peak)

VERDICT: Day 66 is the most positive day for India since the ceasefire on April 8. Project Freedom worked. Iran blinked. Two vessels are safely headed home. The ceasefire is holding under direct operational pressure. Brent is retreating. Sensex surged. If Project Freedom holds for a week without Iranian attack, the oil crisis begins its slow resolution — not because of a deal, but because the US opened Hormuz by force. The question for India is simple: is the government on the phone to Washington right now asking for India-flagged tankers to join Project Freedom? The kharif season depends on the answer.

featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
